answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can work like a trellis: every agent must stake reputation earned through verified, paid work before it can climb to higher-value tasks, so cheap fake identities stay stuck on the lowest ledge. New identities start with a pigment-thin trust score that only thickens after successful, attested jobs; creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand separate work histories, each requiring real compute and real fees. Attackers thus pay the full price of honest participation for every fake, while honest agents compound trust faster than fakes can imitate it.
